q: Materials which have an electrical resistance that lies between the high resistance values of insulators and the low resistance values of metals are called ____.
e: Semiconductors have resistivity values between conductors (metals) and insulators.

q: For example, ____ and silicon are commonly used semiconductors.
e: Germanium and silicon are the most common elemental semiconductors used in electronics.

q: Gallium arsenide(GaAs) and ____ are used as semiconductors.
e: These are examples of compound semiconductors made from two or more elements.

q: They are ____ semiconductors.
e: Semiconductors made of multiple elements, like GaAs, are classified as compound semiconductors.

q: In metals, ____ are the charge carriers.
e: In metallic conductors, only free electrons are responsible for carrying electric current.

q: In the case of semiconductors, both electrons and ____ are the charge carriers.
e: Semiconductor conduction involves the movement of both free electrons and positive holes.

q: A vacancy which is left by an electron in the semiconductor atom is called a ____.
e: When an electron gains enough energy to leave its atom, the resulting vacancy acts as a positive charge carrier.

q: When the potential is applied to two ends of a semiconductor, electrons moves from lower potential to higher one, while the ____ move in the opposite direction.
e: Holes move from higher potential to lower potential, opposite to the direction of electron flow.

q: This means that the current flows due to the movement of ____ in the case of semiconductors.
e: Total current in a semiconductor is the sum of electron current and hole current.

q: Pure semiconductors have ____ of electrons, and positive holes.
e: In an intrinsic (pure) semiconductor, every electron promoted to the conduction band leaves exactly one hole behind.

q: Since these are relatively few in number at normal temperature, pure semiconductors have ____.
e: Intrinsic semiconductors are poor conductors at room temperature due to the low number of charge carriers.

q: When a few ____ are added to the pure semiconductor, its conductivity increases.
e: The process of adding impurities to increase conductivity is called doping.

q: Arsenic, aluminium and ____ atoms are used as impurity atoms.
e: These elements are commonly used as dopants to create n-type or p-type semiconductors.

q: As a result, ____ types of semiconductor are obtained.
e: Doping produces either n-type or p-type extrinsic semiconductors.

q: When arsenic atoms having ____ valence electrons are added to the pure semiconductor (Ge, Si) atoms having four valence electrons, the conductivity of pure semiconductor increases.
e: Pentavalent impurities like arsenic provide an extra free electron for conduction.

q: Since the number of electrons is greater than that of positive holes in this impure semiconductor it is called an ____.
e: The 'n' stands for negative, indicating that electrons are the majority charge carriers.

q: In the n-type semiconductor ____ are the majority charge carriers of electric current.
e: Pentavalent doping introduces excess free electrons, making them the majority carriers.

q: When indium atoms having ____ valence electrons are added to pure semiconductor(Ge, Si) atoms having four valence electrons, the conductivity of pure semiconductor increases.
e: Trivalent impurities like indium create a deficiency of electrons, resulting in holes.

q: Since the number of positive holes is greater than that of electrons in this impure semiconductor it is called a ____.
e: The 'p' stands for positive, indicating that holes are the majority charge carriers.

q: Thus in a p-type semiconductor ____ are the majority charge carriers of electric current.
e: Trivalent doping creates excess holes, making them the majority carriers in p-type material.

q: A boundary or junction is formed between p-type and n-type semiconductors by semiconductor device fabrication process, and this junction is called a ____.
e: The interface between p-type and n-type materials forms the fundamental p-n junction.

q: A device which consists of a p-n junction is called a ____.
e: A diode is the simplest semiconductor device, formed by a single p-n junction.

q: When a battery is joined with its negative terminal to the p-type and its positive terminal to the n-type, only a very small current flows through the p-n junction diode, and it is said to be ____.
e: Reverse bias widens the depletion region, allowing only a tiny minority carrier current to flow.

q: It means that the current flows in ____ only from the anode to the cathode in a vacuum diode and from p to n in a p-n junction diode.
e: This unidirectional current flow is the fundamental rectifying property of a diode.

q: Anode and cathode of a p-n junction, not in connection with a battery, are not at the same electric potential because there is initially a ____ across the junction.
e: A built-in potential barrier exists across the depletion region of an unbiased p-n junction.

q: A rectifier is a device which converts an alternating current (AC) into a unidirectional current or a ____.
e: Rectification is the process of converting bidirectional AC into unidirectional DC.

q: Diodes can be used as rectifiers because the current flows in ____ only from anode to cathode.
e: The unidirectional conduction property of diodes makes them ideal for rectification.

q: The diagram shown in Figure 11.5 (a) is that of a ____.
e: A half-wave rectifier uses a single diode to pass only one half of the AC cycle.

q: There is only ____ diode in the half-wave rectifier circuit.
e: The simplicity of the half-wave rectifier comes from its use of a single diode.

q: As the current I flows in the diode for every first half of the cycle of AC, this device acts as a ____.
e: It is named 'half-wave' because it only utilizes half of the input AC waveform.

q: The circuit diagram shown in Figure 11.6(a) is that of a ____.
e: A full-wave rectifier converts both halves of the AC cycle into pulsating DC.

q: The full-wave rectifier circuit consists of ____ diodes.
e: A center-tapped full-wave rectifier uses two diodes to conduct on alternate half-cycles.

q: Since D1 and D2 operate ____ for one cycle of an AC voltage, current always flows through the resistor R.
e: One diode conducts during the positive half-cycle and the other during the negative half-cycle.

q: As the current flows through R for both half-cycle of the AC voltage, this device is called a ____.
e: It is called 'full-wave' because it utilizes the entire input AC waveform.

q: The principal application of a rectifier is to convert ____.
e: Rectifiers are essential in power supply units to provide DC power from AC mains.

q: Most of the electronic devices require ____ for their operation.
e: Internal electronic circuits in devices like radios and computers operate on direct current.

q: A transistor is a semiconductor device which works as an ____.
e: Transistors are primarily used to amplify weak electrical signals.

q: In ____, three American physicists Shockley, Bardeen and Brattain invented the transistor.
e: The invention of the transistor in 1949 revolutionized modern electronics.

q: A transistor is made of ____ layers of p- and n-semiconductors.
e: A transistor consists of three alternating layers of semiconductor material.

q: There are two common kinds of transistors called the ____ transistors.
e: Transistors are classified by the arrangement of their p-type and n-type layers.

q: In a pnp transistor a thin layer of ____ is sandwiched between two layers of p-semiconductors.
e: The pnp configuration has an n-type base between two p-type regions.

q: In an npn transistor a thin layer of ____ is sandwiched between two layers of n-semiconductors.
e: The npn configuration has a p-type base between two n-type regions.

q: An electrode is attached to each layer and hence there are three electrodes; the ____, the collector (C) and the base (B) in a transistor.
e: The three terminals of a transistor are the emitter, base, and collector.

q: Transistors do not ____ with time, whereas vacuum tubes do.
e: Unlike vacuum tubes, solid-state transistors have a much longer operational lifespan.

q: Transistors are physically much more ____ than vacuum tubes.
e: Solid-state construction makes transistors highly resistant to mechanical shock.

q: Transistors waste much less ____ than vacuum tubes.
e: Transistors are highly energy-efficient compared to the high power consumption of vacuum tubes.

q: There is no ____ after switching on a transistor.
e: Transistors operate instantly, unlike vacuum tubes which require time to heat the cathode.

q: Transistors are very much ____ than vacuum tubes but they perform a similar function.
e: The miniaturization of transistors enabled the development of compact modern electronic devices.

q: In a transistor biasing circuit, a current ____ flows in the collector circuit.
e: $I_C$ represents the collector current, which is the main output current of the transistor.

q: The remainder of positive holes flows into the base so that the current ____ is obtained.
e: $I_B$ is the small base current that controls the much larger collector current.

q: If $I_E$ is a current which flows across the emitter, then ____.
e: Kirchhoff's current law applied to the transistor dictates that the emitter current is the sum of collector and base currents.

q: However, the base is so thin that $I_B \sim 0.02 I_E$ and ____.
e: Because the base is very thin, almost all charge carriers from the emitter reach the collector.

q: Therefore, the small base current $I_B$ can control a very large ____.
e: This control mechanism is the basis for the transistor's amplification capability.

q: Because of this property a transistor can be regarded as a ____.
e: A small change in base current results in a large change in collector current.

q: The resistance of forward-biased emitter junction is ____ and that of reverse-biased collector junction is large.
e: The input (emitter) circuit has low resistance, while the output (collector) circuit has high resistance.

q: Since the electrical power is ____, the power in the emitter side is small whereas the power in the collector side is large.
e: Despite similar current levels, the high resistance of the collector junction results in higher power output.

q: Therefore, the transistor can be regarded as a ____.
e: The transistor delivers more power to the load than is drawn from the input signal source.

q: Because the thickness of the base is about ____ and the base layer of a transistor is thinner than other two layers, the value of base current $I_B$ is very small.
e: The extreme thinness of the base ensures minimal recombination of charge carriers, keeping $I_B$ very small.

q: An arrangement whereby connections of electronic components such as resistors, capacitors and transistors are made is called an ____.
e: Electronic circuits are networks of components designed to perform specific electrical functions.

q: The three groups of the electronic circuit are (i) vacuum tube circuit (ii) transistor circuit and (iii) ____.
e: Integrated circuits represent the most advanced and miniaturized group of electronic circuits.

q: In the integrated circuit, all the electronic components and connections required for an electronic circuit are all made on ____.
e: ICs fabricate all components monolithically on a single piece of semiconductor material, like silicon.

q: Electronic circuits can be divided into two categories, ____.
e: This is the fundamental classification of electronic circuits based on the type of signals they process.

q: Analog electronics involves quantities with ____, and digital electronics involves quantities with discrete values.
e: Analog signals can take any value within a continuous range, unlike discrete digital signals.

q: Digital electronics involves circuits and systems in which there are only ____ possible states.
e: Digital systems operate on binary logic, which has exactly two distinct states.

q: These states are represented by two different voltage levels: a ____ and a LOW (logic 0).
e: In digital logic, a higher voltage level typically represents a binary 1 (HIGH).

q: In digital systems such as computers, combinations of the two states, called ____, are used to represent numbers, symbols, alphabetic characters, and other types of information.
e: Binary codes map combinations of 1s and 0s to meaningful data.

q: The ____ is a way to represent or express numbers.
e: A number system provides a consistent method for writing and interpreting numerical values.

q: There are various types of number systems such as the ____ and the binary numbers system.
e: The decimal system is the standard human counting system, while binary is used by computers.

q: In the decimal number system, the digits ____ represents numbers.
e: The decimal system is base-10, utilizing ten distinct digits.

q: As it uses 10 digits to represent a number, it is also called the ____.
e: The radix or base of the decimal number system is 10.

q: The position of each digit in a decimal number is positive powers of ten that increase from right to left, beginning with ____.
e: The rightmost digit in a decimal number represents the units place, which is $10^0$.

q: The binary number is another way to represent quantities and it has only ____.
e: The binary system uses only 0 and 1 to represent all numerical values.

q: A computer can understand only the ____ state of a switch.
e: Computer hardware fundamentally operates by detecting the presence or absence of electrical signals.

q: These two states are represented by ____.
e: In binary, 'on' is represented by 1 and 'off' is represented by 0.

q: A binary number is a ____.
e: Each position in a binary number has a specific weight based on powers of 2.

q: The right-most bit is the ____ in a binary whole number and its weight is $2^0 = 1$.
e: The LSB has the smallest impact on the overall value of the binary number.

q: The weight increases from right to left by a ____ for each bit.
e: Binary place values progress as $2^0, 2^1, 2^2, 2^3$, and so on.

q: The left-most bit is the ____; its weight depends on the size of the binary number.
e: The MSB has the largest impact on the overall value of the binary number.

q: The term 'bit' is abbreviation of the words ____.
e: A bit is the fundamental unit of information in computing and digital communications.

q: A bit is the ____ of memory or instruction that can be given or stored on a computer.
e: A single bit represents the most basic, indivisible piece of digital data.

q: A bit is either a ____.
e: Binary digits can only hold one of two possible values.

q: A group of ____ like 10100000 is a byte.
e: A byte is the standard unit of data size, consisting of 8 individual bits.

q: ____ form a megabyte (MB).
e: In binary prefixes, a megabyte is defined as 1024 kilobytes.

q: ____ form one gigabyte(GB).
e: A gigabyte is composed of 1024 megabytes.

q: ____ form one terabyte.
e: A terabyte is composed of 1024 gigabytes.

q: A ____ is an electronic device which takes an information from the environment, makes a decision based on that information and then gives out the result.
e: Logic gates are the fundamental building blocks of digital circuits, performing basic logical operations.

q: Logic gates can be built up using ____ of resistors, diodes and transistors.
e: Early logic gates were constructed by wiring individual components together.

q: However, it is more convenient to use small ____.
e: Modern logic gates are fabricated as compact, reliable integrated circuits.

q: The five common logic gates are ____ gates.
c: AND, OR, NAND, NOR and NOT (inverter)
e: These five gates form the basis of all digital logic design.

q: Logic gate can have two or more inputs but only ____.
e: A standard logic gate processes multiple input signals to produce a single logical result.

q: But, NOT gate has only ____.
e: The NOT gate is unique among basic gates as it operates on a single input signal.

q: For a 2-input AND gate, output X is HIGH only when inputs A and B are ____.
e: The AND gate requires all inputs to be true (HIGH) to produce a true (HIGH) output.

q: The Boolean expression for a 2-input AND gate is ____.
e: In Boolean algebra, the AND operation is represented by multiplication or juxtaposition.

q: For a 2-input OR gate, output X is LOW only when both A and B are ____.
e: The OR gate produces a LOW output only if all of its inputs are LOW.

q: The Boolean expression for a 2-input OR gate is ____.
e: In Boolean algebra, the OR operation is represented by addition.

q: For a 2-input NAND gate, output X is LOW only when inputs A and B are ____.
e: A NAND gate is an AND gate followed by a NOT gate, so it outputs LOW only when all inputs are HIGH.

q: The Boolean expression for a 2-input NAND gate is ____.
e: The overline indicates the logical complement (NOT) of the AND operation.

q: For a 2-input NOR gate, output X is HIGH only when both A and B are ____.
e: A NOR gate is an OR gate followed by a NOT gate, so it outputs HIGH only when all inputs are LOW.

q: The Boolean expression for a 2-input NOR gate is ____.
e: The overline indicates the logical complement (NOT) of the OR operation.

q: The NAND gate and NOR gate are popular logic gates because they can be used as ____, that is, they alone can be used in combination to perform the functions of any other types of gates.
e: NAND and NOR gates are functionally complete, meaning any digital circuit can be built using only one of these gate types.

q: The inverter (NOT gate) performs the operation called ____.
e: Inversion, or complementation, flips the logical state of the input signal.

q: The inverter changes one logic level to the ____.
e: A NOT gate outputs a 1 when the input is 0, and a 0 when the input is 1.

q: When a LOW level is applied to its input, a ____ will appear on its output.
e: This demonstrates the inverting nature of the NOT gate.

q: The Boolean expression for a NOT gate is ____.
e: The overline over the variable A denotes the logical NOT operation.
